significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that "the same features and heads perform a reasoning step regardless of the input/output language," while language identity follows an early–middle–late separation; this is a form-(iii) invariance and ordering claim supplemented by a causal circuit claim. It would establish both a phenomenon—cross-lingual preservation of multi-step reasoning—and a mechanism—reuse of reasoning-critical heads and residual features—thereby predicting where language information and reasoning operations should appear across multilingual runs, rather than merely asserting that some shared representation exists. This distinction bears directly on the live alternatives represented by Wendler et al., "Do Llamas Work in English?" (ACL 2024), but a negative result would only reject the proposed universal reuse and clean factorization, not by itself establish English pivoting because language-specific or mixed circuits remain possible; the branches are nevertheless distinguishable despite some ambiguity in "identically." In the topic-substitution check, the generic question of language and intelligence would not license these circuit-invariance and layer-ordering conclusions, so the score comes from the specific hypothesis rather than the topic.

reach.justification: The named reusable handles are the "causal-head Jaccard overlap," "feature-alignment AUC," and "layerwise language-probe accuracy curve," which together could diagnose whether a model separates reasoning content from language identity; these are principally post-hoc auditing tools rather than predictors that fire before a particular reasoning failure. After re-extraction on another multilingual model, the claim predicts a substantive relation—stable cross-language head/feature reuse plus language identity "concentrated in early and late layers"—rather than merely supplying an open-ended procedure for finding an arbitrary new direction. The asserted scope covers multilingual LLMs and multi-step arithmetic and logical reasoning, with likely uptake by interpretability researchers and model auditors, but it does not support a universal claim across modalities, training paradigms, or intelligence generally. Under topic substitution, none of these diagnostics or transferable layerwise predictions follows from merely investigating language and AI intelligence, so the reach is claim-specific.
